blocks.x: Retrieval, features and BI belong on one governed estate, or none of them is trustworthy.

The lakehouse is the AI program's foundation — literally is not a slogan; it is a delivery position. The evidence is consistent across industries — the constraint is rarely technology; it is whether the operating model takes this seriously from sprint one.

items: Unity Catalog-class governance makes AI corpora permission-safe by inheritance.
Cost governance from day one prevents the warehouse-bill surprise at month nine.
A data product registry turns governance into P&L, not committee minutes.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Where exactly does the evidence for each claim live — and can your auditor reach it without a project?
Who signs the go/no-go gate, and what evidence do they require before signing?
Show us a negative result you documented: the discipline is the product.

blocks.x: The failure mode is predictable: enthusiasm funds the demo, budget cycles gate the industrialization, and by the time the governance conversation starts, shadow usage has already created the exposure the review was meant to prevent.

items: Pre-agreed criteria and locked baselines before build; the demo is the least important artifact.
Named owners, run models and escalation paths agreed with the operating team, not for it.
Replay trails, control tests and documentation as artifacts of the build — never reconstructed.

blocks.x: Warehouse spend typically falls 25-40% under disciplined lakehouse migration.
